analysis.title: GS TMT SPEC SALES: Nvidia/AI/Semis debate & flows; Adyen goes to 1 CEO; HPE beat & raise; Crowdstrike; SES & Eutelsat US regs risk
key_insights: Jensen Huang's return as Nvidia president and CEO removed the most acute leadership concern and triggered short covering in semis. The desk says better sentiment is not a clearing event, and investors still have open questions.

SMH is up 15% but only back to Thursday's level after Friday's extreme sell-off. Investors struggle to tell a durable turn from a sharp reversal, and bearish positioning could fuel a painful squeeze for underweights.

Open fundamental issues: cost of capital for neoclouds, datacentre restrictions fears after the Dem sweep, China and BIS regulation risk for semis and memory, oversupply and inference efficiency, and AI revenue needed to justify capex.

The desk separates the tactical bounce from a fundamental recovery. A sustained re-rating depends on rates, credit and financing conditions, datacentre deployment, and Q4 results showing revenue growth at foundation-model companies.

Nvidia regulatory and legal overhang remains. California AG Bonta says the move changes nothing for his probe, and the BIS rule introduced on 19 Nov and the Commerce entity-list addition of Megaspeed add pressure.

Investor feedback is mostly undecided. Bulls cite nobody left to sell and a sentiment-driven bear market. Bears cite China, power and permitting, ROI and token trajectory, and see limited upside above pre-Election levels or toward the 200-dma.

Historical check: in eight instances of Nasdaq up 7% or more in a day over 20 years, the next month averaged +4.40% with a 75% hit rate (6/8). The next day averaged -2.20%. Sample is too small to be a reliable signal.

Flows: HFs were active covering shorts in NVDA, tech and macro expressions while long-only were quiet. After two weeks of heavy long-only supply in NVDA, supply abatement drove much of the move. Desk activity was a 5 out of 10.

ETFs were about 37% of tape volume, the highest since April versus a 5yr avg of 25%. Levered ETFs were about $1 of every $4 of ETF volume, a record share. S&P top-of-book liquidity is about $2mm versus a $11mm 5yr avg.

Derivatives: vols were crushed after the NVDA headlines, but desk flow skewed to vol buying in spread format. A steep topside vol hurdle makes spot up, vol up hard until the market reclaims the 200dma. Year-end SPY call spreads are the preferred upside expression.
HPE beat and raise: FY27 revenue growth guide rose to 27-35% from 13-17%, EPS growth to 27-35% from 16-20%, and FCF to at least $5.5bn from $5.0bn. Record AI systems orders were $4.5bn.
Adyen co-CEO Pieter van der Does steps down at year-end and Ingo Uytdehaage becomes sole CEO. The desk sees no surprise, with focus on delivering guidance and a new CFO starting in Feb.
Intuit fell 13% on 11/20 after 1QFY27 results with weaker Credit Karma trends and lower guidance. GS maintains a Sell rating.
CrowdStrike plans an all-stock acquisition of Zscaler valuing it at about $43.9bn, reflecting the importance of scale and combined network, identity and endpoint telemetry.

FCC proposal to apply reciprocal restrictions on foreign satellite operators is a potential risk for SES and Eutelsat. The desk sees it as probably a negotiating tactic, and it could strengthen Starlink.
Other tech news: Amazon near a $7.5bn deal for AI optimization start-up Decart, a possible analog IC pricing upcycle in Taiwan, and Apple building silicon photonics for data-center chips.

market_movers.rationale: Jensen Huang's reinstatement eased leadership concern and supply abated, but legal, BIS and China questions remain.
Beat and raise with FY27 guidance sharply higher on Cloud & AI margins and record AI orders.
Weaker Credit Karma and guidance cut, with risk to medium-term revenue CAGRs from TurboTax, CK and QuickBooks.
All-stock acquisition of Zscaler at about $43.9bn.
Target of CrowdStrike's all-stock deal valuing it at about $43.9bn.
Closing in on a $7.5bn deal to buy Decart.
SES and Eutelsat face a potential FCC reciprocity rule risk, though the desk sees it as likely a negotiating tactic.

sector_views.rationale: Tactical relief bounce is credible, but fundamental questions on financing, regulation, oversupply and AI ROI remain unresolved.
US reciprocity rules are a risk to SES and Eutelsat but hard to enforce against government functions.

earnings_insights: HPE F4Q reported: storage revenue +34% YoY, record AI systems orders of $4.5bn, networking orders up more than 50%.

HPE FY27 company guidance: revenue growth 27-35% (from 13-17%), EPS growth 27-35% (from 16-20%), FCF at least $5.5bn (from $5.0bn). Cloud & AI growth 30-40% (from 14-18%) with a 14% margin (from 13%).
Intuit 1QFY27 reported: revenue beat of 1.1%, Credit Karma 1.6% miss, 2Q/FY27 guided 3%/1% lower. Company now expects 3.0-7.0% growth versus 10.5-12.6% prior. Stock fell 13% on 11/20.

FCC reciprocity rules for foreign satellite operators.
vol_and_positioning: Vols were under heavy pressure pre-open and the crush accelerated after the NVDA headlines. Desk flows were two-way but skewed to vol buying, particularly in spread format.

Steep topside vol hurdle makes spot up, vol up difficult until the market reclaims the 200dma. Clients were reluctant to chase the rally, but the street is broadly offsides and forced re-risking is possible.
Straddle for the rest of the week went out at 2.15%.
US ETF short flows rose +8.5% Friday and +19% last week, the 3rd largest weekly increase in the past decade.
NDX constituent volumes were up about 60%. ETFs were about 37% of tape, and levered ETFs were a record share of ETF volume.
S&P 500 top of book hovered around $2mm, an intraday ytd low versus a $11mm 5yr avg.
geopolitical: FCC proposal to apply reciprocal restrictions on foreign satellite operators, with SpaceX urging conditions on Eutelsat's pending 528-satellite application.
BIS regulation introduced on 19 Nov and Commerce adding Megaspeed to the entity list create China-related regulatory concerns for semis.
Datacentre restriction fears after the Dem sweep.
